Issue is that "googleapis" is a new_local_repository, not a local_repository (with an associate WORKSPACE file).

Time to try and figure out if there's a reason why.

It looks like `@googleapis` was added by @buchgr in https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/166f28cd620f9fc9c4694242916a7fe1a9a998da.

@buchgr, why is this a new_local_repository instead of a local_repository?

I have changes in progress (it requires a test fix first). Just wanted to be sure there wasn't a deeper reason I'd missed.

Fixes #6601.

body:
I ran into a closely related issue: is it possible to consume the googleapi targets from a downstream repo? As @katre notes above, `bazel build //third_party/googleapis:...` is broken due to incompatible source paths in the .proto files. This means a downstream repo can't consume `@io_bazel//third_party/googleapis:...`. But as far as I know, there is no way for downstream repos to see the local repository `@googleapis` form either.

(Context: I'm trying to consume the Build Event Service protos. Although their canonical home seems to be in the googleapis repo, that repo [doesn't have any build targets at all](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis/tree/master/google/devtools/build/v1) for those protos. The forked versions in the Bazel repo have exactly the targets I want...I just don't know how to consume them.)

Unfortunately, there's no good way for Bazel to make this available directly from our source tree. The ideal solution would be for googleapis to provide their own BUILD files.

You should be able to import a Bazel release as an http_archive, and then give a strip_prefix that, basically, takes out everything except "third_party/googleapis". (Or possibly handle that with a patch on top of the Bazel repository). I haven't tested that, but it might work. It's pretty wasteful on downloads, however.
